specification: Implement path-scoped access control as the package acl, consisting of three editable modules (acl/paths.py, acl/groups.py, acl/acl.py) plus an empty acl/__init__.py that must not be edited. acl/paths.py defines split_path(path), lineage(segments) and join(segments). split_path accepts an absolute resource path and returns a tuple of its segments: it raises TypeError if path is not a str and ValueError if the str does not start with '/'. The path '/' gives the empty tuple. For any other path a single trailing '/' is ignored, so '/a/b/' and '/a/b' both give ('a', 'b'); the remainder is split on '/', and an empty segment (as in '/a//b', '//a', '/a//' or '//') or a segment equal to '.' or '..' raises ValueError. lineage(segments) takes a tuple of segments and returns a list of tuples ordered from the root to the node itself, starting with the empty tuple and ending with the full tuple, each one segment longer than the one before. join(segments) returns the path str '/' followed by the segments joined with '/' (so the empty tuple gives '/'). acl/groups.py defines class Directory, which starts empty and keeps users and nested groups. All names are nonempty strs (TypeError for a non-str, ValueError for an empty str; arguments are checked left to right). add_user(group, user) makes user a direct member of group, creating the group if necessary. add_subgroup(parent, child) makes the group child a member of the group parent, creating either group if necessary; it raises ValueError and changes nothing if child equals parent or if parent is already a member of child directly or through other groups, because that would create a membership cycle; adding a link that already exists is allowed and changes nothing. principals(user) returns a frozenset of strings that contains 'user:' followed by the user name, and, for every group the user belongs to directly or through any chain of group memberships, 'group:' followed by the group name; a user who was never added only has the 'user:' entry. acl/acl.py defines class Acl(directory), which takes a Directory and starts with no rules. grant(principal, path, action, effect, recursive=True) adds a rule. A principal is the str '*' (everyone), or 'user:' or 'group:' followed by a nonempty name. The path is checked with split_path, the action is a nonempty str (the str '*' stands for every action), the effect is the str 'allow' or 'deny', and recursive must be a bool. Checks run in the order principal, path, action, effect, recursive; each argument has its type checked (TypeError) before its value (ValueError, which also covers every error that split_path reports); a call that raises changes nothing. Adding a rule that is identical to an existing one has no further effect. A recursive rule applies to its path and to every descendant of that path; a rule with recursive=False applies only to exactly its own path. revoke(principal, path, action, effect) validates its four arguments exactly like grant, removes every stored rule with that principal, normalized path, action and effect (whatever its recursive flag), and returns the number of rules removed as an int. decide(user, path, action) validates user as in Directory.principals, then path with split_path, then action (a nonempty str, TypeError or ValueError) which must not be '*' (ValueError); a path is compared in normalized form. A rule is relevant to the request if its principal is '*' or one of the user's principals, its action equals the requested action or is '*', and its path is the requested path or one of its ancestors, with a non-recursive rule counting only when its path is exactly the requested path. Among the relevant rules, only those at the deepest path (the one with the most segments) take part in the decision: if any of them has effect 'deny' the request is denied, otherwise it is allowed, so a deeper rule overrides every shallower rule and, on the same path, deny overrides allow regardless of the order in which the rules were added. If there is no relevant rule the request is denied by default. decide returns a dict {'allowed': bool, 'path': the join() of the deciding path or None by default, 'effect': 'allow', 'deny' or None by default}. check(user, path, action) returns the 'allowed' value of decide. Exception messages are not specified.
